issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares the Lecture attributes as private (encapsulated), but the template Lecture.java exposes two attributes as public. The solution uses private fields. This visibility mismatch between the UML/problem statement, the template, and the solution can confuse students about whether to declare attributes as private or public and whether to rely on direct field access or getters/setters.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Lecture.java declare all attributes with the same visibility as shown in the UML (private) and provide getters/setters in the template stubs. Alternatively, if the intention is to have public fields, update the UML and problem statement to reflect public visibility. Prefer updating the template to use private fields to match the UML and the solution so students learn encapsulation.
